question: Should OpenClaw adopt ordered, immutable startup configuration layers as a supported core Gateway CLI and configuration-ownership contract?
rationale: The PR is technically substantial and well demonstrated, but it creates a durable public config composition model whose precedence, mutation, reload, and hosting semantics require maintainer intent rather than automated acceptance.

options.title: Approve after RFC and repair
options.body: Sponsor the core contract, require the write guard to be scoped by canonical config owner, and merge after focused compatibility proof.

options.title: Keep composition external
options.body: Decline the new core surface and continue requiring launchers to materialize one canonical OpenClaw configuration document.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Accept only a smaller supported input mechanism after the RFC defines which precedence, policy-tightening, and immutability semantics belong in core.

recommendation.title: Approve after RFC and repair
recommendation.body: Sponsor the core contract, require the write guard to be scoped by canonical config owner, and merge after focused compatibility proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are directly routed in the PR timeline and have recent context on config-write safety, making them the best available owner for coordinating the product and implementation decision.
